article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Do-Si-Dos × Mendo Breath × Kush
Breeder: Sensi Seeds
THC Content: N/A
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Lemon, pine, roasted nuts, cream, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–75 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 400–450 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500+ g per plant u
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Cashew Kush does not follow the usual dessert strain formula despite being built from some of the most influential American boutique genetics of the past decade. Instead of pushing toward candy, berry syrup, or overpowering fuel, this cultivar develops a fresher profile where lemon and pine sit above cream, earth, and an unusual nutty finish. Sensi Seeds Research created it by crossing Do-Si-Dos and Mendo Breath, then introducing a Kush parent, producing an evenly balanced 50% indica and 50% sativa hybrid with a combination of Cookies-family density, Mendocino sweetness, OG-style depth, and surprisingly open plant architecture.

Its effects follow an equally distinct progression. The first phase can feel lively and almost Haze-like, bringing mental stimulation and an upbeat social quality before the body gradually settles into a longer-lasting state of relaxation. Dense elongated flowers become sticky with resin as the 55–75-day flowering period progresses, while indoor yields can reach approximately 400–450 g/m². Outdoors, well-developed plants can pass 500 grams under favorable conditions. That combination of fresh terpenes, resin production, hybrid effects, and practical cultivation has made Cashew Kush one of the more distinctive releases from the Sensi Seeds Research program.
Genetics and Lineage

The official pedigree is (Do-Si-Dos × Mendo Breath) × Kush. Do-Si-Dos was created by Archive Seed Bank from OGKB × Face Off OG BX1. OGKB is closely associated with the Cookies genetic family , contributing dense flower, sweet dough, resin, and a heavy physical quality, while Face Off OG BX1 reinforces classic OG structure, fuel, spice, and potency. Together they made Do-Si-Dos one of the defining Cookies-meets-OG cultivars of its generation and a natural choice for breeding projects that need both trichome production and substantial body effects.

Mendo Breath adds another important American genetic branch. Its direct parents are OGKB and Mendo Montage, linking Cookies-associated genetics with Mendocino breeding. Mendo Montage itself combines Mendo Purps with Crystal Locomotive, a line carrying Trainwreck and Aloha White Widow influence. That background helps explain the creamy, earthy, slightly sweet qualities associated with Mendo Breath while also introducing additional resin potential and a softer, more rounded character than a conventional OG hybrid.

Sensi Seeds then crossed the Do-Si-Dos × Mendo Breath foundation with a Kush parent. The breeder does not identify that Kush more precisely in the current catalog, so assigning a specific Kush cultivar would be inaccurate. Its contribution is nevertheless easy to recognize in the finished plant: sturdy branches, earthy undertones, dense resinous flowers, and a physically relaxing second half to the experience. The completed hybrid therefore concentrates OGKB influence through both Do-Si-Dos and Mendo Breath while widening the pedigree with Face Off OG, Mendocino genetics, Trainwreck-related ancestry, White Widow influence, and additional Kush material.
Effects and Experience

Cashew Kush begins on a surprisingly bright note. The first noticeable shift can feel mentally stimulating, upbeat, and socially comfortable, with a cerebral buzz that Sensi Seeds compares to selected Haze varieties. Conversation may flow more easily, music can become more absorbing, and low-pressure creative activities may feel more engaging. The effect has movement without becoming especially frantic, which distinguishes it from narrow-leaf sativas that can produce a sharper or more restless kind of stimulation.

That mental lift gradually gives way to a more grounded physical state. Instead of an abrupt drop into sedation, body relaxation builds underneath the cerebral effect until the two overlap. The result can feel peaceful rather than immobilizing: shoulders loosen, physical tension becomes less prominent, and the desire to rush from one task to another fades. Moderate servings may remain suitable for relaxed social settings, while larger amounts emphasize the Kush and Mendo Breath sides and produce a much more settled experience.

Sensi Seeds does not publish a standardized THC figure for Cashew Kush, which is preferable to attaching one laboratory result to an entire seed line. Potency can vary with phenotype, lighting, nutrition, harvest timing, and testing methodology. Consumers should therefore judge the actual flower rather than relying on an assumed number. Excessive intake of THC-rich marijuana can still produce dry mouth, dizziness, mental fog, or temporary anxiety, particularly if the initially uplifting phase encourages repeated consumption before the heavier body effect arrives.
Medical Benefits

The change from cerebral stimulation to physical calm may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a cultivar with more than one stage to its effects. During the earlier portion of the session, the uplifting headspace may make everyday stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less intrusive. Because the initial phase can remain relatively clear and social, some consumers may find moderate amounts easier to integrate into late-afternoon routines than weed that becomes sedating from the first inhalation.

Later, the heavier body component becomes more relevant. General muscle tension and everyday discomfort may fade further into the background as relaxation develops, while stronger servings may encourage appetite or make quiet rest more appealing. The balanced genetic structure means the cultivar is not defined solely by couchlock, but the second half can still become substantially more physical than the opening suggests. Timing and dose therefore play an important role in whether the experience feels functional or deeply relaxing.

No standardized CBD level or complete laboratory terpene profile is published for the line. Medical use should consequently be based on testing from the specific harvest whenever possible, especially for consumers who need predictable cannabinoid ratios. Personal THC sensitivity, prescription medications, serving size, and previous reactions to marijuana remain more useful than assuming the strain name guarantees a specific therapeutic outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Lemon and pine form the most immediately recognizable part of the aroma. During flowering, the plant begins releasing a relatively clean combination of citrus and evergreen rather than an overwhelmingly sweet or skunky odor. After drying and curing, those notes become more defined and take on a sparkling quality, with fresh lemon sitting above a crisp pine background. The profile feels considerably fresher than its dense Kush-heavy genetics might suggest.

The deeper layers emerge once the flower is broken apart. Earth appears underneath the citrus, while nutty and creamy notes introduce the character responsible for the Cashew name. The nuttiness does not necessarily resemble raw cashews in a literal sense; it is closer to a rich roasted quality mixed with cream, earth, and sweet Kush. Mendo Breath contributes softness, while the Do-Si-Dos side adds resinous depth and traces of dough and OG funk.

On the palate, citrus and pine generally arrive first, followed by creamier, earthier flavors through the middle of the inhale. The exhale can reveal more of the roasted-nut character, leaving behind a smooth combination of pine, sweet earth, and Kush. Vaporization tends to preserve the lemon and fresh upper notes particularly well, whereas combustion emphasizes the richer earthy and nutty finish. A slow cure rewards patience by allowing those contrasting layers to separate instead of collapsing into generalized sweetness.
Growing Information

Cashew Kush displays both halves of its 50/50 genetic balance in the garden. Vegetative growth is steady rather than explosive, and plants can remain fairly restrained until flowering begins. Once the light cycle changes, stretch increases substantially and internodal spacing opens, producing a medium-to-tall plant with good airflow through the canopy. Indoors, finished height is generally around 100–150 cm, while outdoor plants commonly reach 150 cm or more when given adequate root space and sunlight.

Flowering takes approximately 55–75 days. Indoor yields commonly reach 400–450 g/m² across soil, coco, hydroponics, and living-soil systems. Dense elongated buds develop along sturdy lateral branches, and resin production becomes heavy enough that trimming can quickly coat scissors and gloves. The relatively open structure reduces the need for aggressive defoliation, although selective pruning and canopy management can still improve light penetration. SOG , SCROG , supercropping, and lollipopping are all suitable approaches, giving experienced growers several ways to shape the plant around their available space.

Outdoors, Cashew Kush prefers a warm, sunny environment with a long summer, particularly Mediterranean-style climates. Under optimal conditions, plants can produce 500 grams or more each. Sensi Seeds does not provide one universal outdoor harvest date because flowering onset varies by latitude, but the 55–75-day bloom provides a useful guide once reproductive growth begins. Mature flowers finish light green against darker foliage, creating a striking visual contrast beneath a substantial trichome coating.
FAQ
What strains make Cashew Kush?
Cashew Kush was created by Sensi Seeds Research from Do-Si-Dos × Mendo Breath, followed by a cross with Kush. Do-Si-Dos is OGKB × Face Off OG BX1, while Mendo Breath comes from OGKB × Mendo Montage.
Is Cashew Kush indica or sativa?

Sensi Seeds classifies the cultivar as an even 50% indica and 50% sativa hybrid. Its effects reflect that balance, beginning with an uplifting cerebral phase before developing into a longer-lasting relaxing body sensation.
How long does Cashew Kush take to flower?

Indoor flowering takes approximately 55–75 days. The exact harvest point depends on phenotype and growing conditions, so flower development, pistil maturity, and trichome appearance should be considered alongside the calendar.
What does Cashew Kush taste like?

Its flavor combines lemon and pine with earth, sweet cream, and a distinctive roasted-nut quality. The fresher citrus and pine notes tend to lead, while the creamy, nutty Kush character becomes more noticeable on the finish.
How much does Cashew Kush yield?
Indoor production commonly reaches approximately 400–450 g/m². Outdoors, plants can exceed 500 grams each under optimal warm and sunny conditions with sufficient root space.
Final Thoughts on Cashew Kush

Cashew Kush is a useful example of modern American genetics being interpreted through a European breeding program without losing their original character. Do-Si-Dos contributes OGKB and Face Off OG influence, Mendo Breath brings Mendocino depth and additional OGKB ancestry, and the final Kush parent reinforces structure, resin, earth, and physical relaxation. The completed cross is genetically complex, but its identity remains surprisingly focused.

Cultivation performance is equally balanced. Plants stretch enough during flowering to create an open canopy yet retain the sturdy branching required to support dense, sticky buds. A 55–75-day bloom, indoor production of roughly 400–450 g/m², and outdoor yields exceeding 500 grams per plant give this cannabis strain serious garden value without making it particularly difficult to manage. Its compatibility with soil, coco, hydroponics, living soil, SOG, SCROG, supercropping, and lollipopping adds further flexibility.

What ultimately distinguishes the strain is the contrast between its aroma and its pedigree. Rather than overwhelming fuel or sugary Cookies terpenes, the flower develops fresh lemon and pine above cream, earth, and roasted-nut richness. The experience follows a similar pattern of contrast, starting with a Haze-like cerebral lift before settling into a peaceful Kush-influenced body stone. Cashew Kush offers a distinctive interpretation of contemporary cannabis breeding: resinous, productive, mentally lively at first, physically calming later, and flavored with enough nutty depth to justify a name that initially sounds almost improbable.
